lines.text: Your model's likelihood takes minutes to compute.
You want the posterior over its parameters.
The posterior tells you how plausible each setting is, given your data.
Picture the posterior as a landscape.
The higher the ground, the more plausible the setting.
The textbook method is Markov chain Monte Carlo.
It needs tens of thousands of evaluations.
At a few minutes each, you would wait weeks.
Bayesian optimization finds the highest point of a landscape in far fewer evaluations.
It learns the landscape from the points it has seen, then decides where to look next.
Pie V B M C does the same for the whole posterior.
lines.caption: PyVBMC does the same for the whole posterior.

lines.text: We start in the dark.
Each evaluation reveals the height at a single point.
From these few points, Pie V B M C builds a surrogate.
lines.caption: From these few points, PyVBMC builds a surrogate.

lines.text: The surrogate is a cheap statistical model of the whole landscape.
At the evaluated points it holds still.
Everywhere else it wobbles.
The more it wobbles, the less it knows.
On the surrogate, Pie V B M C fits a mixture of Gaussians.
lines.caption: On the surrogate, PyVBMC fits a mixture of Gaussians.

lines.text: This is its first guess at the posterior.
For now it is a crude one.
Where to evaluate next?
An optimizer would head for the peak.
Pie V B M C is after the whole posterior, so it looks for places that are plausible and still uncertain.
lines.caption: PyVBMC is after the whole posterior, so it looks for places that are plausible and still uncertain.

lines.text: Evaluate.
Update the surrogate.
Refit the mixture.
Round after round, the wobbling dies down.
The mixture grows new components to follow the ridge.
Pie V B M C never saw the true landscape.
lines.caption: PyVBMC never saw the true landscape.

lines.text: Here it is.
Pie V B M C also estimated the model's evidence.
lines.caption: PyVBMC also estimated the model's evidence.

lines.text: You need that number to compare two models.
The estimate lands close to the true value.
All this from a hundred evaluations.
Markov chain Monte Carlo would have needed tens of thousands.
Weeks of waiting became an afternoon.
